main.after: Guarded IN-ARCP has low acquisition probability under idealized continuous migration.

main.before: Adaptive and AR-whitening detectors restore scale invariance (Section~\ref{sec:related}), but take their thresholds from Gaussian laws or simulation, whose tail accuracy on real clutter is rarely measured.
main.after: Adaptive covariance and AR-whitening detectors restore scale invariance under their model assumptions (Section~\ref{sec:related}). This does not establish the accuracy of model-based thresholds in the far tail of measured clutter.

main.before: On IPIX these thresholds hold the rate to $10^{-4}$ and on NetRAD S-band sea clutter to $10^{-3}$, where the model-based laws of most whitened detectors and of the adaptive normalized matched filter (ANMF) fail.
main.after: On IPIX and NetRAD, these thresholds improve measured tail calibration over the tested model-based laws, including those of the adaptive normalized matched filter (ANMF); NetRAD retains failures at $10^{-4}$.

main.before: We test the framework on IPIX, NetRAD S-band sea clutter unused in development, and 77~GHz FMCW data with real interference, against the PAMF, ANMF, power detectors, certified trimming and pulse blanking. The per-look test shares the PAMF's whitening gain. Its contribution here is a framework that calibrates false alarms on real clutter, quantifies target self-masking and certifies integration under interference.
main.after: We evaluate tail calibration on X-band IPIX and S-band NetRAD sea clutter; NetRAD was unused in initial development and its thresholds are refitted. Injected onsets, longer trajectories and continuous migration test sensitivity to reference contamination. Two 77~GHz FMCW datasets provide real interference and pedestrian returns, with detector-external camera labels in the University of Washington (UW) recordings. Comparators include PAMF, ANMF, power detectors, certified trimming and pulse blanking. The per-look score shares the PAMF's whitening gain.

main.before: We found no such analysis for the AR-innovation score of a cell's own history.
main.after: We found no such analysis for the AR-innovation score of a cell's own history. Motion-aware coherent integration searches jointly over range and velocity \cite{xu2011rft}. Our migration study tests whether the cell-wise history-normalized score remains useful when crossing time is unknown.

main.before: The laws follow a target through the detector, from the tested pulse at onset to a target that persists into the history and a dwell of several pulses; the calibration and certification of the threshold close the section.
main.after: We first establish the onset law, then quantify history contamination and dwell integration before calibrating and certifying thresholds.

main.before: \emph{Protocols.} Methods, settings, metrics and expected outcomes were recorded in hashed protocols before computing outcomes. The Supplementary Material reports data exposure, failed conditions, deviations and exploratory analyses.
main.after:
\emph{Camera-labelled pedestrians.} Three UW 77~GHz records acquired in 2019 provide raw ADC frames and external camera labels \cite{uwraw2022,gao2021ramp}. One fixed chirp/transmit/receive channel per frame supplies range-bin slow time; whole-record training/calibration/test rotations and camera-screened clutter masks are fixed before scoring (Supplementary Material).

\emph{Protocols.} Methods and expected outcomes were recorded before computation. The Supplementary Material identifies data exposure, failed conditions and exploratory choices.

supplement.before:
The paper's evidence covers neither the middle nor any operational scan pattern,
so no intermediate look rate can yet be recommended.
supplement.after: The UW study adds intermediate frame spacing, but its weak correlation and empty primary clean-entry set leave correlated-clutter onset detection unvalidated (Section~\ref{sup:uw}). No operational scan pattern or useful intermediate look rate is established.
